knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For a portfolio with claim frequency as Y and age and territory as X, which statement correctly assigns response and explanatory roles with a one-sentence justification?
knowledge_checks.body: Select Y, X, and actuarial warrant for a frequency model.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For frequency modelling, claim frequency is Y and rating factors such as age and territory are X. Column-soup or reversed roles ignore the modelling question.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Response = claim frequency (Y). Explanatory = age, territory (X). Justification: model frequency as outcome explained by rating factors.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Column-soup modelling or treating every numeric field as an explanatory variable without naming Y first.

choices.label: Response Y = claim frequency (the outcome to model). Explanatory variables X = age and territory (rating factors thought to explain or predict frequency). Justification: we model frequency as the outcome explained by rating factors.
Response Y = age; explanatory variables are claim frequency and territory because every column in the portfolio table is a predictor.
Age and territory are both response variables; frequency is an explanatory variable because it is numeric.
Response and explanatory roles cannot be named until a multiple regression equation is written; the portfolio sketch is insufficient.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Motor book: you want to model claim severity. Columns include age, sum insured, claim amount, NCD discount, and claim count. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Name Y and warranted X variables; refuse column-soup.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For severity modelling, claim amount is Y. Age and sum insured are plausible X's with warrants. Claim count is a different outcome type. Column-soup is not role assignment.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Y = claim amount (severity). X examples: age, sum insured. Refuse column-soup.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting column-soup or treating claim count as automatically an X for severity.

choices.label: Response Y = claim amount (severity, the outcome to explain). Explanatory examples: age and sum insured (predictors of severity with a one-sentence warrant each). Claim count is a frequency outcome, not automatically an X for severity. Putting every numeric column on the right-hand side is not variable-role modelling.
Response Y = claim count; explanatory variables are claim amount, age, sum insured, and NCD because all numeric columns belong on the right-hand side.
Response Y = claim amount; claim count must also be an explanatory variable because it appears in the same policy record as severity.
No response can be named until a multiple regression equation is fully written; severity modelling starts with equation form, not Y versus X.

worked_example.title: Assign Y and X, then evaluate an EL severity line
worked_example.problem_statement: An employers' liability pricing analyst models claim severity (£). The fitted simple linear relationship from a pilot sample is ŷ = 2500 + 150x, where x is years in a hazardous occupation class. (a) Name the response and the explanatory variable. (b) Compute the fitted mean severity at x = 8.

given.note: years in hazardous class for the prediction

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Name Y and X in one sentence, then substitute x = 8 into ŷ.

steps.label: Assign response and explanatory roles
steps.attempt_cue: State which quantity is Y and which is X.
steps.explanation: The modelling question is claim severity, so severity is the response Y. Years in the hazardous class is the predictor used to explain severity, so that tenure measure is the explanatory variable X.
steps.calculation: Y = EL claim severity (£); X = years in hazardous occupation class

steps.label: Evaluate the fitted mean at x = 8
steps.explanation: Once roles are fixed, the fitted line gives the modelled mean response at a chosen X value.

steps.label: Refuse column-soup
steps.attempt_cue: State why written premium is not automatically an X for severity.
steps.explanation: Written premium is a pricing output (or input to another model). Sharing a policy record with severity does not make it an automatic explanatory variable for a severity model.
steps.calculation: Written premium is not auto-X for severity by column presence alone
steps.result: Roles fixed by the modelling question, not by column presence

worked_example.final_answer: Y = EL claim severity, X = years in hazardous occupation class; ŷ(8) = £3700. Written premium is not automatically an explanatory variable for severity.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating every numeric policy field (including written premium or headcount) as an explanatory variable for severity, or swapping roles so that hazardous-class years are modelled as Y and severity as X.
